claim: A valid extreme elevation ramp can overflow the squared gradient and panic or be misclassified instead of producing a cliff.
trigger: Provide a dry source elevation field at 1:1 compression with a 3×3 cell corner profile [i32::MIN, i32::MAX, i32::MAX, i32::MIN] centimeters, and sample a tile whose edge rise passes the earlier steepness filter.
expected_vs_actual: The steep cell should be classified without panicking. Here rise_x is about 4,294,967,295, whose square exceeds i64; overflow-checked builds panic, while release arithmetic wraps and can make the comparison return None.
evidence: crates/map/src/environment.rs:190-200 accepts any i32 heights when page dimensions are valid; crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:80-82 computes the unsaturated squared gradient.

votes.evidence: The documented behavior says “Elevation steeper than a 35% source grade is still impassable Cliff terrain without a sprite” (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:108-109). ElevationPage::validate checks dimensions and sample count but places no bound on i32 heights (environment.rs:189-200). For the stated 1:1 extreme profile, rise_x can exceed 3,037,000,499, so squaring it at relief.rs:82 overflows; the aoe-map test profile enables overflow checks (Cargo.toml:40-43), causing a panic before a tile is returned.

crates/map/src/environment.rs:189-200 validates elevation page dimensions and length but accepts i32::MIN and i32::MAX heights. With 1:1 compression, the stated profile passes relief.rs:64, then rise_x is 4,294,967,295; relief.rs:82 squares it in i64, which overflows in checked builds and panics during terrain sampling.

claim: The start reservation is checked per tile, so a cliff cell can cross into the reserved glade or connector and still draw its full sprite there.
trigger: A valid dry, camera-facing contour cell straddles the glade or connector boundary, with its anchor outside the reservation and another cell tile inside it.
expected_vs_actual: The docs define a cliff as one three-by-three cell and require it to be “dry land outside the starting glade and its connector.” The whole cell should be excluded; instead, only reserved tile queries return None, while the unreserved anchor can still create a sprite over reserved ground.

votes.evidence: The per-tile reservation check at `crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:98-101` also applies to the connector, so an eligible cell can cross either reservation boundary and still emit a face from an unreserved anchor. This overlaps F6’s glade-boundary case.

crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:98-101 checks whether the current tile is reserved, not whether the whole three-by-three cell is reserved. If the anchor is outside the glade or connector while another cell tile is inside, queries/chunks.rs:198-207 still emits the sprite on the anchor, so it can overlap the reserved area.

claim: The documented sprite-free behavior above a 35% source grade is not enforced by cliff detection.
trigger: A dry 50% planar slope falls toward the camera, a three-tile cell crosses an 8 m contour, the pass noise is at least 116, and the cell is outside the start reservation.
expected_vs_actual: The docs say elevation above a 35% source grade remains impassable Cliff terrain “without a sprite.” `cliff_at` has a minimum steepness check but no maximum-grade check, so this cell can produce and draw a cliff sprite.

votes.evidence: The behavior defect is real: `crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:82-96` has a minimum steepness test but no maximum-grade rejection, and `chunks.rs:198-207` can emit a sprite for a qualifying Cliff tile. A 50% slope can meet the contour and pass conditions described. Since this violates the explicit sprite-free requirement at `docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:108-109` on realistic steep terrain, Major severity fits better than Minor.

docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:108-109 says slopes above 35% remain sprite-free. crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:82-109 has no maximum-grade check, so a dry, camera-facing contour cell on a 50% slope can still return a cliff piece for rendering.

claim: Cliff placement depends on the procedural seed through the starting connector, contrary to the geography-only requirement.
trigger: Generate the same elevation field with the same geography key but two procedural seeds whose starting connectors differ; at a dry, cliff-eligible tile in only one connector, this check suppresses the cliff for that seed.
expected_vs_actual: The same geography should produce the same cliff terrain across seeds; instead, cliff classification changes with the connector’s seed-dependent path.
evidence: The requirement says relief depends on geography only, never the procedural seed (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:85-86); starting_connector_contains builds Patches with generator.procedural_seed (crates/map/src/terrain/landscape.rs:79). The new test also excludes a broad central area from its seed comparison (crates/map/src/terrain/tests/mountains/cliffs.rs:90-93).

votes.evidence: `crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:98-101` makes cliff eligibility depend on the per-tile connector reservation. That connector is seed-dependent: `crates/map/src/terrain/landscape.rs:79-89` constructs `Patches` with `generator.procedural_seed`. Thus the same geography can receive different cliff classification across seeds; the comparison test masks a broad central area at `crates/map/src/terrain/tests/mountains/cliffs.rs:90-93`.

The stated requirement is “depend on the geography only (never on the procedural seed)” (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:85-86). relief.rs:98-99 checks the per-tile connector, which constructs Patches with generator.procedural_seed (landscape.rs:79). Thus an otherwise eligible tile can change cliff classification across seeds; the seed comparison test masks the central area (cliffs.rs:90-93).

claim: The composer can emit cliff sprites on wet tiles because this new decoration path does not check the tile’s water kind.
trigger: A provider-backed tile has non-None water, steep source corners that leave its surface kind as Cliff, and a cliff-eligible anchor; cliff_piece_with_cancel evaluates relief without checking water.
expected_vs_actual: Cliff pieces are restricted to dry land; the composer emits a Cliff decoration on the wet tile, which the renderer draws as a face over water.
evidence: The changed guard checks surface kind and piece eligibility but not base.water (crates/map/src/terrain/landscape/queries/chunks.rs:198-200). The documented eligibility condition is “dry land” (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:106).

votes.evidence: `crates/map/src/terrain/landscape/queries/chunks.rs:198-200` checks surface kind and piece eligibility, but not water. A wet provider tile can retain `SurfaceKind::Cliff` from `surface::from_heights` on an excessive source grade (`crates/map/src/terrain/surface.rs:98-105`); water resolution can leave that surface intact when there is no modeled surface level (`crates/map/src/terrain/provider/water_model.rs:120-128`). The composer can then emit a cliff decoration over water.

The eligibility requirement is “dry land outside the starting glade and its connector” (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:106). Provider terrain can retain SurfaceKind::Cliff from steep source corners (provider.rs:39-46); categorical water without a modeled surface does not replace that surface (provider/water.rs:157-181). The new composer path checks Cliff and piece eligibility but not water (queries/chunks.rs:198-207), so an eligible wet anchor can receive a cliff decoration.

claim: The starting-area exclusion is evaluated per tile, so a cliff cell crossing the glade boundary can be only partly impassable while still receiving a whole-cell sprite.
trigger: A three-by-three cliff-eligible cell straddles the starting-glade boundary, with its anchor outside the glade and other tiles inside it.
expected_vs_actual: A cliff piece should cover one consistently impassable three-by-three cell and stay clear of the glade; instead, this per-tile check excludes only the in-glade tiles, while the outside anchor can still emit the face.
evidence: The eligibility check passes the individual tile to starting_glade (crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:98); the documented piece is a three-by-three cell of impassable ground with its sprite on the centre tile (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:87-90).

votes.evidence: `crates/map/src/terrain/relief.rs:98-101` checks reservations for the individual tile. An unreserved anchor can therefore pass, while reserved tiles in the same cell are not marked Cliff; `crates/map/src/terrain/landscape/queries/chunks.rs:198-207` then emits the whole-cell sprite.

The documented piece is “a three-by-three tile cell of impassable ground” carrying one sprite on its centre tile (docs/geodata/landscape/implementation.md:87-90). relief.rs:98-99 applies the glade and connector exclusions to the individual tile. A cell crossing the boundary can therefore have excluded tiles and an eligible outside anchor that emits the whole-cell sprite.
